newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar closes firmer on bond strength.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar closes firmer on bond strength.

text.p: * Canada's dollar closed much stronger at C$1.3407 (US$0.7459) from Tuesday's close of C$1.3440 (US$0.7441), drawing its strength from North American bond markets and a bullish report on the Canadian currency from Goldman Sachs, dealers said.
* They said the unit started to move after higher than expected Q3 gross domestic product numbers from the U.S.
Canadian bonds followed U.S. bonds higher on Wednesday after the U.S. government reported that gross domestic product (GDP) rose 2.2 percent in the third quarter.
The Canadian bond market ended the day outperforming the U.S. market on Wednesday with the 30-year benchmark bond rising C$0.20 to C$110.90 to yield 7.083 percent.
The Canadian dollar also broke through a key technical point of C$1.3430 on Wednesday, helping it to move firmer, dealers said.
On the crosses, the Canada rose to 1.1266 marks from Tuesday's 1.1233 marks and rose to 85.11 yen from 85.04 yen.
